title: What the Warranty and Safety Recall Coverage Does Not Cover: Wear, Damage, Aftermarket Parts and Outside Maintenance
content:
# What Is Not Covered, Aftermarket Parts and Outside Maintenance

These terms of the Warranty and Safety Recall Coverage apply to claims under any coverage type according to that coverage type's exclusion and condition settings.

## Terms

**Wear items.** Where the coverage type's wear-items exclusion is Yes, wear items (brake pads and rotors, wiper blades, tires, filters, bulbs) are not covered.

**Environmental and other damage.** Where the coverage type's environmental-damage exclusion is Yes, damage from hail, flood, fire or road salt is not covered, nor is damage from collision, abuse or neglect.

**Aftermarket and recycled parts.** Where the coverage type's aftermarket-parts setting is Yes, installing aftermarket or recycled parts never voids a coverage; a claim is rejected for an aftermarket part only when that part caused the failure, with the reason aftermarket part caused failure.

**Maintenance outside the group.** Where the coverage type's independent-maintenance setting is Yes, maintenance done at any shop or by the owner satisfies the maintenance requirement when it is documented; a claim is never rejected because the maintenance was not done at a group store.

## The same terms by question

| Question | Answer where the setting is Yes |
|---|---|
| Are brake pads, rotors, wiper blades, tires, filters or bulbs covered? | No |
| Is hail, flood, fire or road-salt damage covered? | No |
| Is damage from collision, abuse or neglect covered? | No |
| Does fitting an aftermarket or recycled part void the coverage? | Never |
| Can a claim be rejected because of an aftermarket part? | Only when that part caused the failure |
| Does documented maintenance at an independent shop, or by the owner, meet the maintenance requirement? | Yes |
| Can a claim be rejected because maintenance was not done at a group store? | Never |

## Hypothetical cases

- A vehicle fitted with an aftermarket air filter has a covered engine part fail for a reason unrelated to the filter. The aftermarket part is no ground to reject the claim.
- An aftermarket part is found to have caused the failure. The claim is rejected with the reason aftermarket part caused failure, and the coverage itself remains in force.
- The owner changed the oil personally and kept receipts for every service. That documented maintenance satisfies the maintenance requirement.
